name: recall
description: Ask the learner to EXPLAIN something in his own words — a graded check with NO options: he types a free-text answer. Unlike ask_user_question (no right answer), recall always has one. THE COMMITMENT RULE: correctAnswer is the FULL correct answer in your own words, reasoning included, COMMITTED before he ever sees the question. When his answer returns, grade it strictly against the commitment — never revise it after seeing his words. He sees the committed answer on submit. ONE question per turn: call a single recall, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

question.description: The single question to ask. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next.

correctAnswer.description: REQUIRED. The full correct answer in your own words, reasoning included — COMMITTED before the learner ever sees the question. The commitment is immutable: when his answer returns, grade it strictly against this text — never revise the commitment after seeing his words, and never mark a wrong answer right to be kind. It is shown to him on submit; your next reply grades the nuance of what he wrote.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the learner a single question and pause until they answer. NOT graded — there is no correct answer. Use when requirements are ambiguous, preferences are needed, a decision would materially affect the lesson, or you need an open-ended response. ONE question per turn: call a single ask_user_question, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

question.description: The single question to ask the learner. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next question.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

label.description: Display label for the answer option — a bare claim, no reasoning

value.description: Optional machine-readable value returned for the option. Defaults to the label.

description.description: Optional extra detail shown below the option

options.description: Optional multiple-choice options. Omit for free-form text input. The learner can always choose 'Other' and type a custom answer when options are provided.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow multiple answers to the same question.

name: read
description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

name: ls
description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: the learner's home directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

name: find
description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Ignores node_modules, .git, and Library directories. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: the learner's home directory)

name: grep
description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Ignores node_modules, .git, and Library directories. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50.0KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: the learner's home directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

name: research
description: Dispatch a background web-research agent: fact verification, current data, or niche specifics you are not certain about. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the research brief arrives later as a new message and the lesson resumes from it. Cite the brief's sources when you use them. NEVER use it for things you know cold, internal reasoning, or math.

question.description: The single research question to answer. Make it specific — the researcher sees nothing else of the lesson.

context.description: Why you need this / what the lesson needs it for — focuses the brief. One or two sentences.

name: pdf
description: Dispatch a background sub-agent that READS a learner-provided PDF on your behalf (triage, targeted extraction, visual page reading for equations and diagrams) and returns a brief with page citations. Use it when the learner gives you a PDF path and you need its CONTENT for the lesson. The call is ASYNC and fire-and-forget — it resolves immediately and your turn continues; the brief arrives later as a new message. For quick looks at plain text or image files, use the read tool directly instead of dispatching.

path.description: Path to the learner's PDF (relative or absolute), exactly as they gave it.

question.description: What you need from the document — the specific content, explanation, or answer to extract and brief. The reader sees NOTHING else of the lesson.

name: list_sessions
description: List the sessions of the learner's persistent knowledge graph — every chat or imported-notes file that ever contributed a proposition, most recent first. The map is organized into birth-session clusters (propositions grouped by the session they were first learned in), and session names are those clusters' labels. Each line: the session's name, kind (chat/file), how many propositions were born in it, its dates, and its id — use that id with list_propositions. Reading this first shows what he has already covered and when, before you probe anything.

name: list_propositions
description: List the propositions BORN in one knowledge-graph session — what was covered there. Names only — no statement text, no session contents (owner ruling 2026-09-23: the map's ORGANIZATION is your business, its prose is not).

session.description: The session's id exactly as list_sessions reported it (a chat id or a notes source id)

name: probe_done
description: Conclude the probing phase and hand off to the teaching phase. Call this ONCE, when the probe is complete: every strand the lesson depends on is bracketed (a floor he reliably gets right AND a ceiling where it runs out), and his learning goal is concrete. The input IS the learner assessment — one strand per dependency the lesson will rest on, with your read of where his edge sits on it (floor, ceiling, misconceptions, what to build from). It streams to the learner live and becomes the handoff artifact the teacher plans from. Refused while a question is still open, and after the probe is already concluded. After it succeeds, say your closing sentence and end your turn.

strand.description: The dependency strand (e.g. 'the derivative as a limit') — a name the plan can hang a node on.

assessment.description: Where his edge sits on this strand: the floor (what he reliably gets right), the ceiling (where it runs out), misconceptions found, and what the lesson should build from.

strands.description: Every strand the planned lesson will depend on, each with your read of his edge on it.

summary.description: Optional overall synthesis: his apparent goal and where the teaching should enter.

assessment.description: The learner assessment — the probe's distilled output.
